Caffeine contributes to endurance performance, apparently 
because of its ability to enhance mobilization of fatty acids and 
thus conserve glycogen stores. Caffeine also may directly affect 
muscle contractility, possibly by facilitating calcium transport. 
It could reduce fatigue as well by reducing plasma potassium 
accumulation, which contributes to fatigue. An energy-enhancing 
effect is seen with up to 3 mg/kg body mass or about 200 mg 
caffeine for the 150-lb athlete (Spriet, 2014). Unwanted side
